skill.name: running-tests
skill.description: Helps detect project test commands, run test suites, report failures, and guide follow-up fixes.
skill.summary: Detects and runs project tests, then summarizes failures and verification results.
skill.author: 1gy

security_audit.summary: All six static detections are false positives because the backticks are Markdown formatting for test command examples, not executable Ruby or shell code. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, or secret access was found in SKILL.md. One low-severity workflow risk remains because the skill tells the agent to commit fixes without an explicit approval gate.

remediation.issue: Automatic commit step lacks an explicit approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before creating commits, and report the planned files and commit message first.

remediation.issue: Local test commands can execute project scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should run this skill only in trusted repositories or isolated environments.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 is a Markdown table row with inline command text, not executable Ruby or shell code. It documents a standard Node test command mapping.
Line 17 is Markdown documentation for a Rust test command. The backticks are formatting and do not create shell execution by themselves.
Line 18 lists a Just test command in a Markdown table. There is no Ruby backtick evaluation, interpolation, or hidden executable code.
Line 19 documents a Make test command using inline Markdown code. The syntax is explanatory text, not code that executes automatically.
Line 20 is a Markdown command example for Python tests. The backticks are presentation markup and do not indicate shell execution in the file.
Line 21 is a Markdown table entry for Go tests. It contains no executable Ruby or shell backtick expression.

content.value_statement: Finding the right test command can slow verification across languages. This skill detects common test setups, runs tests, reports failures, and guides fixes.
actual_capabilities: Reads project guidance to find a documented test command.
Detects common test files and maps them to standard commands.
Runs the selected test command through the available shell tool.
Reports pass or fail status, failed test names, and error messages.
Analyzes test failures and identifies likely implementation, test, or environment causes.
Reruns tests after fixes to confirm the result.
limitations: It depends on project files and documentation to choose a command.
It may need user input when no test command is detected.
It cannot guarantee tests are safe in untrusted repositories.
It does not replace a full CI pipeline or security sandbox.

use_cases.title: Verify Feature Changes
use_cases.description: Run local tests after code changes and get a concise failure report.

use_cases.title: Triage Failing Suites
use_cases.description: Classify failures as code, test, or environment issues before review.

use_cases.title: Prepare CI Handoffs
use_cases.description: Check common project test commands before a pull request or deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the running-tests skill to find the project test command, run it, and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the running-tests skill to run tests, list failed test names, and explain the likely cause.

prompt_templates.title: Fix and Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the running-tests skill to run tests, fix failures from code or tests, and rerun until resolved.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a CI Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the running-tests skill to detect the command, execute it, classify failures, and produce a completion report.

output_examples.input: Run the tests for this project.
output: Detected the Node test command from package metadata.

Next step: investigate the changed parsing behavior.

output_examples.input: The test suite is failing. Find the cause.
output_examples.output: The skill reports failed test names, relevant error messages, and whether the likely cause is code, tests, or environment.

output_examples.input: Verify the fix before I open a pull request.
output: Tests were rerun after the fix.
The completion report includes final status, test count, and applied changes.

best_practices: Run this skill only in repositories you trust or can safely sandbox.
Add the preferred test command to project guidance for consistent detection.
Review failure summaries before accepting automated fixes or commits.
anti_patterns: Running tests in unknown repositories without inspecting project scripts.
Treating an environment failure as a code defect.
Skipping the final rerun after making a fix.

faq.question: Which test frameworks can it detect?
faq.answer: It checks common project files for Node, Rust, Just, Make, Python, and Go test commands.

faq.question: Will it ask before running tests?
faq.answer: It asks when no test command is found. Users should request confirmation for untrusted projects.

faq.question: Can it fix failing tests?
faq.answer: It can guide fixes when failures indicate implementation or test issues, then rerun tests to verify.

faq.question: Does it commit changes?
faq.answer: The source instructions mention committing fixes. Confirm repository policy before allowing commits.

faq.question: Does it replace CI?
faq.answer: No. It helps local verification, but CI remains the authority for controlled build and test environments.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted code?
faq.answer: No local test runner is fully safe for untrusted code. Use a sandbox or isolated machine.
